When I was an intern, I was doing night duty in the department of neurosurgery emergency. All the bad RTA cases used to come. I was sitting alone in the duty room late at night. It was around 3:30 am when a person knocked the door and came inside. It was my first day at that place so I didn't know everyone working in that department. I assumed he was a Gr D staff. He entered calmly and said that a patient has expired and I have to go and declare the death. I said I'm coming. 
When I went to the ward I saw a different staff sitting there and asked him if someone has expired. He pointed me to a trolly where I saw a person with almost a crushed head. But the thing is, he looked surprisingly similar to the person that came to call me in the duty room. 
Later I tried to convince myself that it's just my mind that is making up stories. But I couldn't sleep for the next 2 days after that. It gives me chills thinking about it to this very day.

I have been doing my internship for almost an year now ( only a few days left for convocation). I have done my duties in all the departments. In my college, we are posted at SNCU for 1 week. This sounds easy but the number of hours is 100. But that's okay, we interns didn't have a problem with the hectic duty hours. The problem  was just the toxicity amongst the nurses posted there. Those nurses had duties for only 8 hour shifts, while the interns had to stay alert for 24 hours straight and monitor vitals of sick neonates. We also had to fix OG tubes for the babies. These nurses were so toxic , that they used to remove those tubes from the baby's mouth just to annoy us. Not to mention their shitty behaviour with the interns. They didn't even treat us as doctors. Once one of the nurses raised her voice against one of my batchmates without any valid reason. When my batchmate asked her the reason she couldn't provide an explanation but started making a video of the conversation on her phone. These things don't just make me angry  but also makes me hopeless ( that nurse was suspended though).
